analysis.investment_thesis: Azad Engineering is a high-quality precision aerospace components maker, but at 101x P/E and an earnings yield of just ~1.3% (EBIT ₹161 Cr / EV ~₹12,520 Cr), the Magic Formula ranks this near the bottom on cheapness. With ROCE at 12.2% — well below my 20% hurdle — and five consecutive years of negative free cash flow, you are paying an extraordinary price for capital that isn't yet earning its keep.
key_strengths: Revenue growing at 38.8% CAGR (2021–2025) with operating margins expanding to 30%+ — rare in Indian industrials.
Niche aerospace/defense precision machining with global OEM customers creates genuine switching-cost moat.
Low D/E of 0.21 and rising equity base (₹1,479 Cr) after IPO provides runway for capex-heavy expansion.
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~1.3% is catastrophically below the Magic Formula's 6% floor — nearly all future growth is priced in.
Free cash flow has been negative every single year (-₹240 Cr in FY25); capex (₹293 Cr) eclipsed EBITDA (₹164 Cr) in FY25.
ROCE of 12.2% and ROE of 8.57% are well below my 20%+ threshold — capital deployment is not yet value-accretive.
red_flags: Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) ≈ 1.3% — among the worst possible Magic Formula scores; extreme overvaluation.
Capex ₹293 Cr vs. EBITDA ₹164 Cr in FY25: the company is burning far more cash than it generates operationally.
Finance costs spiked to ₹52 Cr in FY23 and ₹47 Cr in FY24, suppressing net profit — ₹8 Cr net profit on ₹252 Cr revenue in FY23.
CWIP jumped to ₹155 Cr and investing CF hit -₹918 Cr in FY25 — growth is real but capital intensity is extreme.
ROE of only 8.57% at a 101x P/E multiple is deeply inconsistent; the market is pricing in a business that doesn't yet exist.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Azad Engineering produces two failing grades. Earnings Yield = EBIT ₹161 Cr ÷ EV ~₹12,520 Cr = ~1.3% — I need at least 12% to get interested. Return on Capital (proxied by ROCE) = 12.2%, well below my 20% hurdle. The business scores poorly on both axes of the formula simultaneously, which is the clearest possible AVOID signal. EV/EBITDA of 62x and P/S of 21.6x confirm the market has pre-paid for 10+ years of flawless execution.

The underlying business is genuinely exciting — 5-year revenue CAGR of 38.8%, a defensible niche in safety-critical aerospace components, 30%+ operating margins, and credible global OEM relationships. But the capital intensity is a structural drag: free cash flow has been negative in all five reported years, and FY25 capex alone (₹293 Cr) exceeded total EBITDA (₹164 Cr). Until ROIC crosses 20% and the business begins generating meaningful positive FCF, this remains a growth story priced for perfection at valuations the Magic Formula simply cannot endorse. I would revisit at earnings yield >6% (implying EV closer to ₹2,700 Cr) — roughly an 80% discount to today's price.
